audioscript.text: Hello, Tourist Information Center.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Mike speaking.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: How can I help you?
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Oh, hi.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I wanted to find out about cookery classes.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I believe there are some one-day classes for tourists.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, they're open to everyone, but tourists are always welcome.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: OK, let me give you some details of what's available.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: There are several classes, one very popular one is at the Food Studio.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: OK, they focus on seasonal products, and as well as teaching you how to cook them, they also show you how to choose them.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q1: The passage says they *'show you how to choose them'* — **'choose'** is the word you need. So the answer is **choose**.

audioscript.text: Right, that sounds good.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: How big are the classes?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I'm not sure exactly, but they'll be quite small.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And could I get a private lesson there?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN
audioscript.explain: Q2: The woman asks *'could I get a private lesson'* and the man confirms *'they do offer those'*. So the answer is **private**.

audioscript.text: I think so.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Let me check.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Yes, they do offer those.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q2: The woman asks *'could I get a private lesson'* and the man confirms *'they do offer those'*. So the answer is **private**.

audioscript.text: Though in fact most of the people who attend the classes find it's a nice way of getting to know one another.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: I suppose it must be, yes.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: And this company has a special deal for clients,
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: where they offer a discount of 20 percent, if you return for a further class.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q3: The passage says they offer *'a discount of 20 percent'* if you return. So the answer is **20 percent**.

audioscript.text: OK, but you said there were several classes.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Another one you might be interested in is Bond's Cookery School.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: They're quite new.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: They just opened 6 months ago, but I've heard good things about them.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: They concentrate on teaching you to prepare healthy food, and they have quite a lot of specialist staff.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q4: The passage says Bond's Cookery School *'concentrate on teaching you to prepare healthy food'*. So the answer is **healthy**.

audioscript.text: So is that food for people on a diet, and things like that?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I don't know if I'd be interested in that.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, I don't think they particularly focus on low calorie diets or weight loss.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: It's more to do with recipes that look at specific needs, like including ingredients that will help build up your bones and make them stronger, that sort of thing.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q5: The passage says recipes include ingredients to *'help build up your bones and make them stronger'*. So the answer is **bones**.

audioscript.text: I see.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, I might be interested, I'm not sure.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Do they have a website I could check?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Yes, just key in the name of the school, it'll come up.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And if you want to know more about them, every Thursday evening they have a lecture at the school.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q6: The passage says *'every Thursday evening they have a lecture at the school'* and it's free. So the answer is **lecture**.

audioscript.text: It's free, and you don't need to book or anything, just turn up at 7:30.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And that might give you an idea of whether you want to go to an actual class.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at question 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: OK, there's one more place you might be interested in.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: That's got a rather strange name.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: It's called The Arretsa Center.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q7: The passage says *'It's called The Arretsa Center'* and spells it *'ARRETSA'*. So the answer is **Arretsa**.

audioscript.text: That's spelled ARRETSA.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q7: The passage says *'It's called The Arretsa Center'* and spells it *'ARRETSA'*. So the answer is **Arretsa**.

audioscript.text: OK, they've got a very good reputation.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: They do a bit of meat and fish cookery, but they mostly specialize in vegetarian dishes.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q8: The passage says they *'mostly specialize in vegetarian dishes'* — **'dishes'** means **'food'**. So the answer is **vegetarian**.

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: That's certainly an area I'd like to learn more about.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I've got lots of friends who don't eat meat.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: In fact, I think I might have seen that school today.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Is it just by the market?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN
audioscript.explain: Q9: The woman asks *'Is it just by the market?'* and the man says *'That's right'*. So the answer is **market**.

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q9: The woman asks *'Is it just by the market?'* and the man says *'That's right'*. So the answer is **market**.

audioscript.text: So they don't have any problem getting their ingredients.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: They're right next door.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And they also offer a special two-hour course in how to use a knife.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q10: The passage says they offer *'a special two-hour course in how to use a knife'*. So the answer is **knife**.

audioscript.text: They cover all the different skills, buying them, sharpening, chopping techniques.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: It gets booked up quickly though, so you'd need to check it was available.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Right, well, thank you very much.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I'll go and check that out.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 1.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Section 2.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear the chairman of the Highways Committee of Granford speaking to members of the public about proposed changes to traffic and parking in the area.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 13.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 13.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Good evening everyone.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: My name is Phil Sutton, and I'm chairman of the Highways Committee.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We've called this meeting to inform members of the public about the new regulations for traffic and parking we're proposing for Granford.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: I'll start by summarizing these changes before we open the meeting to questions.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: So, why do we need to make these changes to traffic systems in Granford?
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: Well, we're very aware that traffic is becoming an increasing problem.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: It's been especially noticeable with the increase in heavy traffic while they've been building the new hospital.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: But it's the overall rise in the volume of traffic of all kinds that's concerning us.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q11: The passage says *'the overall rise in the volume of traffic of all kinds that's concerning us'* — **'rise in the volume'** means the **amount** has **increased**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: To date, there's not been any increase in traffic accidents.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: But that's not something we want to see happen, obviously.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: Uh. We recently carried out a survey of local residents, and their responses were interesting.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: People were very concerned about the lack of visibility on some roads due to cars parked along the sides of the roads, we'd expected complaints about the congestion near the school, when parents are dropping off their children or picking them up.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q12: The passage says people were *'very concerned about the lack of visibility... due to cars parked along the sides of the roads'* — **'cars parked'** means **inconvenience from parked cars**. ***They expected complaints about school congestion, but that was not top of the list***. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: But this wasn't top of the list, and nor were noise and fumes from trucks and lorries, though they were mentioned by some people.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We think these new traffic regulations would make a lot of difference, but we still have a long way to go.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We've managed to keep our proposals within budget, just.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: So they can be covered by the Council, but of course it's no good introducing new regulations if we don't have a way of making sure that everyone obeys them.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q13: The passage says *'it's no good introducing new regulations if we don't have a way of making sure that everyone obeys them'* — **'obeys'** means **follow**. So the problem is **finding a way to make people follow them**. The answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: And that's an area we're still working on with the help of representatives from the police force.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 14 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 14 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: OK, so this slide shows a map of the central area of Granford, with the High Street in the middle and School Road on the right.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: Now we already have a set of traffic lights in the High Street at the junction with Station Road, but we're planning to have another set at the other end at the School Road junction.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says they are planning *'another set at the other end at the School Road junction'* — the map shows **School Road** meeting the High Street at point **E**. So the new traffic lights are at **E**.

audioscript.text: To regulate the flow of traffic along the High Street.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We've decided we definitely need a pedestrian crossing.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We considered putting this on School Road just outside the school.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: But in the end, we decided that could lead to a lot of traffic congestion.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: So we decided to locate it on the High Street, crossing the road in front of the supermarket.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says they decided to locate the pedestrian crossing *'on the High Street, crossing the road in front of the supermarket'* — the supermarket on the map is at point **D**. So the answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: That's a very busy area, so it should help things there.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: We are proposing some changes to parking.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: At present, parking isn't allowed on the High Street outside the library.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.text: But we are going to change that and allow parking there, but not at the other end of the High Street near School Road.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON
audioscript.explain: Q16: The passage says they will *'allow parking there'* outside the library — the library on the map is at point **B**. So parking allowed is at **B**.

audioscript.text: There'll be a new no parking sign on School Road.
audioscript.speaker: PHIL SUTTON

audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear two biology students called Emma and Jack discussing an experiment they are going to do together.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: We've got to choose a topic for our experiment, haven't we, Jack?
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Were you thinking of something to do with seeds?
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Hmm, that's right.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I thought we could look at seed germination, how a seed begins to grow.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: OK, any particular reason?
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: I know you're hoping to work in plant science eventually.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Yeah, but practically everything we do is going to feed into that.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: No, there's an optional module on seed structure and function in the 3rd year that I might do, so I thought it might be useful for that.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q21: Jack says *'there's an optional module on seed structure and function in the 3rd year that I might do, so I thought it might be useful for that'* — this means he may study a **related topic** later. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: If I choose that option, I don't have to do a dissertation module.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: Good idea.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Hmm, well I thought for this experiment, we could look at the relationship between seed size and the way the seeds are planted.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: So we could plant different sized seeds in different ways and see which grow best.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: OK, we'd need to allow time for the seeds to come up.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: That should be fine if we start now.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q22: Emma says *'A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer'* and Jack agrees *'that would make it a good one to choose'* — so the main advantage is it can be **completed in the time available**. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: So that would make it a good one to choose.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA
audioscript.explain: Q22: Emma says *'A lot of the other possible experiments need quite a bit longer'* and Jack agrees *'that would make it a good one to choose'* — so the main advantage is it can be **completed in the time available**. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: And I don't suppose it needs much equipment.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: We're not doing chemical analysis or anything, though that's not really an issue.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: We've got plenty of equipment in the laboratory.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Yeah, we need to have a word with the tutor if we're going to go ahead with it though.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I'm sure our aim's OK, it's not very ambitious, but the assignment's only 10% of our final mark, isn't it?
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: But we need to be sure we're the only ones doing it.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q23: Jack says *'we need to be sure we're the only ones doing it'* — **'the only ones'** means no one else has chosen it. So they check with the tutor whether **anyone else has chosen this topic**. The answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Yeah, it's only 5% actually, but it would be a bit boring if everyone was doing it.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Did you read that book on seed germination on our reading list?
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: The one by Graves?
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Hmm, I looked through it for my last experiment, though it wasn't all that relevant there.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: It would be for this experiment though, I found it quite hard to follow, lots about the theory which I hadn't expected.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA
audioscript.explain: Q24: Jack says he found the book *'quite hard to follow, lots about the theory which I hadn't expected'* — **'lots about the theory'** means its **focus is very theoretical**. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Yes, I'd been hoping for something more practical.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: It does include references to the recent findings on genetically modified seeds, though.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: Yes, that was interesting.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: I read an article about seed germination by Lee Hall.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: About seeds that lie in the ground for ages and only germinate after a fire.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Hmm, that's the one.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I knew a bit about it already, but not about this research.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: His analysis of figures comparing the times of the fires and the proportion of seeds that germinated was done in a lot of detail, very impressive.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q25: Jack says *'His analysis of figures... was done in a lot of detail, very impressive'* — **'analysis of figures'** means **analysis of statistics**, and **'in a lot of detail'** means it is **thorough**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Was that the article with the illustrations of early stages of plant development?
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: They were very clear.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: I think those diagrams were in another article.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: We'll need to get going with it quite soon.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: So the first thing we have to do is find our seeds.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I think vegetable seeds would be best, and obviously they mustn't all be the same size.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q26: Emma says they need vegetable seeds and *'obviously they mustn't all be the same size'* — so they must select seeds of different **types** and sizes. The answer is **G**.

audioscript.text: So how many sorts do we need?
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: About four different ones.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I think that would be enough.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: There'll be quite a large number of seeds for each one.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: Then for each seed, we need to find out how much it weighs.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q27: Jack says *'for each seed, we need to find out how much it weighs'* — so they measure and record the **weight**. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: And also measure its dimensions, and we need to keep a careful record of all that.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: That'll be quite time consuming, and we also need to decide how deep we're going to plant the seeds.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA
audioscript.explain: Q28: Jack says *'we also need to decide how deep we're going to plant the seeds'* and lists options like *'a few millimeters down, or several centimeters'* — so they decide on the **depths** to be used. The answer is **H**.

audioscript.text: Right on the surface a few millimeters down, or several centimeters.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA
audioscript.explain: Q28: Jack says *'we also need to decide how deep we're going to plant the seeds'* and lists options like *'a few millimeters down, or several centimeters'* — so they decide on the **depths** to be used. The answer is **H**.

audioscript.text: OK, so then we get planting.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: Do you think we can plant several seeds together in the same plant pot?
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: No, I think we need a different one for each seed.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA
audioscript.explain: Q29: Jack says *'I think we need a different one for each seed'* — **'a different one'** means a different **container** (plant pot). The answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Hmm, right, and we'll need to label them.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: We can use different colored labels.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: Then we wait for the seeds to germinate.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: I reckon that'll be about 3 weeks, depending on what the weather's like.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: Then we see if our plants have come up.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: And write down how tall they've grown.
audioscript.speaker: JACK
audioscript.explain: Q30: Emma says after 3 weeks they will *'write down how tall they've grown'* — **'how tall'** means the plant's **height**. The answer is **E**.

audioscript.text: Then all we have to do is look at our numbers and see if there's any relation between them.
audioscript.speaker: EMMA

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: So then we...
audioscript.speaker: JACK

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 3.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

audioscript.text: Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear part of a lecture on an environmental studies course about recent research on how animals are adapting to urban environments.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Hi. Today we're going to be looking at animals in urban environments, and I'm going to be telling you about some research on how they're affected by these environments.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Now, in evolutionary terms, urban environments represent huge upheavals, the sorts of massive changes that usually happen over millions of years.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And we used to think that only a few species could adapt to this new environment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One species which is well known as being highly adaptable is the crow.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says *'One species which is well known as being highly adaptable is the crow'* — the question asks for an example of a highly adaptable animal. So the answer is **crow**.

audioscript.text: And there have been various studies about how they manage to learn new skills.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Another successful species is the pigeon.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Because they're able to perch on ledges on the walls of city buildings, just like they once perched on cliffs by the sea, but in fact we're now finding that these early immigrants were just the start of a more general movement of animals into cities.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says pigeons perch on city buildings *'just like they once perched on cliffs by the sea'* — so city walls are similar to **cliffs** for them. The answer is **cliffs**.

audioscript.text: And of adaptation by these animals to city life.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And one thing that researchers are finding especially interesting is the speed with which they're doing this.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage says researchers find the *'speed'* of adaptation especially interesting — **'speed'** means how fast something happens. So the answer is **speed**.

audioscript.text: We're not talking about gradual evolution here.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These animals are changing fast.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Let me tell you about some of the studies that have been carried out in this area.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, in the University of Minnesota, a biologist called Emilie Snell-Rood.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And her colleagues looked at specimens of urbanized small mammals such as mice and gophers that had been collected in Minnesota, and that are now kept in museums there.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And she looked at specimens that had been collected over the last hundred years, which is a very short time in evolutionary terms.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And she found that during that time, these small mammals had experienced a jump in brain size when compared to rural mammals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says Snell-Rood found *'a jump in brain size'* in urban mammals — **'jump'** here means an increase. So the answer is **brain**.

audioscript.text: Now we can't be sure this means they're more intelligent.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But since the sizes of other parts of the body didn't change, it does suggest that something cognitive was going on.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And Snell-Rood thinks that this change might reflect the cognitive demands of adjusting to city life.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Having to look in different places to find food for example, and coping with a whole new set of dangers.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage explains the brain change might be from *'having to look in different places to find food'* — this means locating new sources of **food**. So the answer is **food**.

audioscript.text: Then over in Germany at the Max Planck Institute, there's another biologist called Catarina Miranda, who's done some experiments with blackbirds living in urban and rural areas.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: She's been looking not at their anatomy, but at their behavior.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The passage says Miranda looked *'not at their anatomy, but at their behavior'* — **'behavior'** is what animals do. So the answer is **behaviour**.

audioscript.text: So as you might expect, she's found that the urban blackbirds tend to be quite bold.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They're prepared to face up to a lot of threats that would frighten away their country counterparts, but there's one type of situation that does seem to frighten the urban blackbirds.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And that's anything new, anything they haven't experienced before.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says urban blackbirds are frightened by *'anything new, anything they haven't experienced before'* — so they fear **new** situations. The answer is **new**.

audioscript.text: And if you think about it, that's quite sensible for a bird living in the city.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Jonathan Atwell in Indiana University is looking at how a range of animals respond to urban environments.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: He's found that when they're under stress, their endocrine systems react by reducing the amount of hormones such as corticosterone into their blood.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says *'when they're under stress'*, animals reduce hormones — the question asks what causes lower hormone levels. So the answer is **stress**.

audioscript.text: It's a sensible-seeming adaptation.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: A rat that gets scared every time a subway train rolls past won't be very successful.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: There's just one more study I'd like to mention, which is by Sarah Partan and her team.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And they've been looking at how squirrels communicate in an urban environment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And they found that a routine part of their communication is carried out by waving their tails.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The passage says squirrels communicate by *'waving their tails'* — they use their **tails** to send signals. So the answer is **tail**.

audioscript.text: You do also see this in the country, but it's much more prevalent in cities.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Possibly because it's effective in a noisy environment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So what are the long-term implications of this?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One possibility is that we may see completely new species developing in cities, but on the other hand, it's possible that not all of these adaptations will be permanent.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says *'it's possible that not all of these adaptations will be permanent'* — **'permanent'** means lasting forever. So the answer is **permanent**.

audioscript.text: Once the animals got accustomed to its new environment, it may no longer need the features it's developed.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So now we've had a look...
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

utterances.text: OK, so this meeting is for new staff and staff who haven't been involved with our volunteering projects yet.

utterances.text: So basically the idea is that we allow staff to give up some of their work time to help on various charity projects to benefit the local community.

utterances.text: We've been doing this for the last five years.

utterances.text: And it's been very successful.

utterances.text: Participating doesn't necessarily involve a huge time commitment.

utterances.text: Obviously, many people will have family commitments and aren't as available as other members of staff.

utterances.text: They also liked building relationships with the people in the local community, and felt valued by them.

utterances.text: One or two people also said it was a good thing to have on their CVs.

utterances.text: One particularly successful project last year was the Get Working project.

utterances.text: This was aimed at helping unemployed people in the area get back to work.

utterances.text: Our staff were able to help them improve their telephone skills, such as writing down messages and speaking with confidence to potential customers, which they had found quite difficult.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: This is something many employers look for in job applicants, and something we all do without even thinking about every day at work.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: We've got an exciting new project starting this year.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: Up until now, we've mainly focused on projects to do with education and training, and we'll continue with our reading project in schools.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: And our work with local charities, but we've also agreed to help out on a conservation project in Redfern Park.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER
utterances.explain: Q14: The passage says a new project is *'a conservation project in Redfern Park'* — a **park** is the place for this project. So the answer is **B**.

utterances.text: So, if any of you fancy being outside and getting your hands dirty, this is the project for you.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: I also want to mention the annual Digital Inclusion Day, which is coming up next month.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: The aim of this is to help older people keep up with technology.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: And this year, instead of hosting the event in our own training facility, we're using the ICT suite at Hill College, as it can hold far more people.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER
utterances.explain: Q15: The passage says *'instead of hosting the event in our own training facility, we're using the ICT suite at Hill College'* — so the location is a **college**. So the answer is **B**.

utterances.text: We've invited over 60 people from the Silver Age Community Center to take part, so we'll need a lot of volunteers to help with this event.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: If you're interested in taking part, please go to the volunteering section of our website and complete the relevant form.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER
utterances.explain: Q16: The passage says *'please go to the volunteering section of our website and complete the relevant form'* — **'complete the relevant form'** means **fill in a form**. So the answer is **A**.

utterances.text: We won't be providing any training for this.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: But you'll be paired with an experienced volunteer if you've never done it before.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: By the way, don't forget to tell your manager about any volunteering activities you decide to do.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Section 3.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear a student called Russ consulting his tutor about a presentation he is preparing on nanotechnology, the study of materials on an extremely small scale.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Ah... come in, Russ.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Thank you.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Now you wanted to consult me about your class presentation on nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You're due to give it next week, aren't you?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That's right, and I'm really struggling.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I chose the topic because I didn't know much about it, and wanted to learn more.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: But now I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS
audioscript.explain: Q21: Russ says *'I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say'* and then asks whether to give a general introduction or focus on one aspect — this shows he is unsure about his goal. **'Uncertainty about what he should try to achieve'** matches this confusion. ***His problem is not lack of knowledge*** — he actually knows too much. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: I could talk for much longer than the 20 minutes I've been allocated.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Should I assume the other students don't know much, and give them a kind of general introduction, or should I try and make them share my fascination with a particular aspect?
audioscript.speaker: RUSS
audioscript.explain: Q21: Russ says *'I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say'* and then asks whether to give a general introduction or focus on one aspect — this shows he is unsure about his goal. **'Uncertainty about what he should try to achieve'** matches this confusion. ***His problem is not lack of knowledge*** — he actually knows too much. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: You could do either, but you'll need to have it clear in your own mind.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Then I think I'll give an overview.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: OK, now one way of approaching this is to work through developments in chronological order.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Uh huh.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: On the other hand, you could talk about the numerous ways that nanotechnology is being applied.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You mean things like thin films on camera displays to make them water-repellent,
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: and additives to make motorcycle helmets stronger and lighter.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Exactly.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Or another way would be to focus on its impact in one particular area.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q22: The tutor suggests *'to focus on its impact in one particular area'*, and Russ replies *'Perhaps I should do that'* — they both agree. This matches option **A**: *'concentrate on how nanotechnology is used in one field'*. ***The other options were mentioned but not chosen***. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Say medicine or space exploration.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That would make it easier to focus.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS
audioscript.explain: Q22: The tutor suggests *'to focus on its impact in one particular area'*, and Russ replies *'Perhaps I should do that'* — they both agree. This matches option **A**: *'concentrate on how nanotechnology is used in one field'*. ***The other options were mentioned but not chosen***. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Perhaps I should do that.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS
audioscript.explain: Q22: The tutor suggests *'to focus on its impact in one particular area'*, and Russ replies *'Perhaps I should do that'* — they both agree. This matches option **A**: *'concentrate on how nanotechnology is used in one field'*. ***The other options were mentioned but not chosen***. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: I think that would be a good idea.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: How important is it to include slides in the presentation?
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: They aren't essential by any means, and there's a danger of tailoring what you say to fit whatever slides you can find.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: While it can be good to include slides, you could end up spending too long looking for suitable ones.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You might find it better to leave them out.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q23: The tutor warns that looking for slides can take too long and says *'You might find it better to leave them out'* — **'leave them out'** means **'omit'**. This directly matches option **C**: *'consider omitting slides altogether'*. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: I see.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Another thing I was wondering about was how to start.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I know presentations often begin with, first, I'm going to talk about this, and then I'll talk about that.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: But I thought about asking the audience what they know about nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: That would be fine if you had an hour or two for the presentation, but you might find that you can't do anything with the answers you get.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: And it simply eats into the short time that's available.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: So maybe I should mention a particular way that nanotechnology is used to focus people's attention.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS
audioscript.explain: Q24: Russ suggests *'mention a particular way that nanotechnology is used to focus people's attention'* — this is giving a specific example. The tutor says *'That sounds sensible'*, so they agree. Option **C**: *'to provide an example'* matches this idea. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: That sounds sensible.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: What do you think I should do next?
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I really have to plan the presentation today and tomorrow.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Well, initially, I think you should ignore all the notes you've made.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Take a small piece of paper and write a single short sentence that ties together the whole presentation.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q25: The tutor says *'write a single short sentence that ties together the whole presentation'* — this means to **summarise** the main point. Option **A**: *'summarise the main point he wants to make'* is a direct match. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: It can be something as simple as, nanotechnology is already improving our lives.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Then start planning the content around that.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You can always modify that sentence later if you need to.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: OK, now let's think about actually giving the presentation.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You've only given one before, if I remember correctly, about an experiment you've been involved in.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: It was pretty rubbish.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Let's say it was better in some respects than in others.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: With regard to the structure, I felt that you ended rather abruptly without rounding it off.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q26: The tutor says Russ *'ended rather abruptly without rounding it off'* — **'without rounding it off'** means it **lacked a conclusion**. This matches comment **A**: *'lacked a conclusion'*. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Be careful not to do that in next week's presentation.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: And you made very little eye contact with the audience, because you were looking down at your notes most of the time.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q27: The tutor says Russ *'made very little eye contact with the audience'* because he looked at his notes — this means the eye contact was **not enough**. This matches comment **C**: *'not enough'*. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: You need to be looking at the audience and only occasionally glancing at your notes.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Hmm. Your body language was a little odd.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Every time you showed a slide, you turned your back on the audience, so you could look at it.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You should have been looking at your laptop, and you kept scratching your head, so I found myself wondering when you were next going to do that, instead of listening to what you were saying.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q28: The tutor mentions Russ kept *'scratching your head'*, which made the tutor wonder when he would do it again instead of listening — this was **sometimes distracting**. This matches comment **D**: *'sometimes distracting'*. So the answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: Oh, dear.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: What did you think of the language?
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I knew that not everyone was familiar with the subject, so I tried to make it as simple as I could.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Yes, that came across.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You used a few words that are specific to the field, but you always explained what they meant, so the audience wouldn't have had any difficulty understanding.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q29: The tutor says Russ used some specific words but *'always explained what they meant'*, so the audience understood — this means the language was **not too technical**. This matches comment **G**: *'not too technical'*. So the answer is **G**.

audioscript.text: Uh-huh.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I must say the handouts you prepared were well thought out.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q30: The tutor says the handouts were *'well thought out'* and people could *'refer to later on'* — this means they will be **useful in the future**. This matches comment **B**: *'useful in the future'*. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: They were a good summary of your presentation, which people would have been able to refer to later on.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q30: The tutor says the handouts were *'well thought out'* and people could *'refer to later on'* — this means they will be **useful in the future**. This matches comment **B**: *'useful in the future'*. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: So well done on that.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Thank you.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Well, I hope that helps you with next week's presentation.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, it will.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: Thanks a lot.
audioscript.speaker: RUSS

audioscript.text: I'll look forward to seeing a big improvement then.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 3.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear a lecturer in psychology talking about a type of memory.

audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Today, we'll be continuing the series of lectures on memory by focusing on what is called episodic memory, and what can happen if this is not working properly.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Episodic memory refers to the memory of an event or episode.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Episodic memories allow us to mentally travel back in time.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To an event from the past.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Episodic memories include various details about these events, for example, when an event happened.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And other information, such as the location.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says episodic memories include details like *'the location'* — the question asks for a detail alongside **time**. So the answer is **location**.

audioscript.text: To help understand this concept, try to remember the last time you ate dinner at a restaurant.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The ability to remember where you ate, who you were with and the items you ordered are all features of an episodic memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Episodic memory is distinct from another type of memory called semantic memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This is the type of factual memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That we have in common with everyone else.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is your general knowledge of the world.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says semantic memory is *'your general knowledge of the world'* — **'general knowledge'** matches **'general information'** in the question. So the answer is **world**.

audioscript.text: To build upon a previous example, remembering where you parked your car is an example of episodic memory, but your understanding of what a car is.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And how an engine works are examples of semantic memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Unlike episodic memory, semantic memory isn't dependent on recalling personal experiences.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage says semantic memory *'isn't dependent on recalling personal experiences'* — this means it does **not** involve **personal** information. So the answer is **personal**.

audioscript.text: Episodic memory can be thought of as a process with several different steps of memory processing: encoding, consolidation and retrieval.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The initial step is called encoding.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This involves the process of receiving and registering information, which is necessary for creating memories of information or events that you experience.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The degree to which you can successfully encode information depends on the level of attention you give to an event while it's actually happening.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says encoding success *'depends on the level of attention you give to an event'* — more **attention** means better encoding. So the answer is **attention**.

audioscript.text: Being distracted can make effective encoding very difficult.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Encoding of episodic memories is also influenced by how you process the event.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For example, if you were introduced to someone called Charlie.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage gives an example of remembering *'Charlie's name'* by using a connection strategy — the thing you want to remember is a **name**. So the answer is **name**.

audioscript.text: You might make the connection that your uncle has the same name.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Future recollection of Charlie's name is much easier.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage gives an example of remembering *'Charlie's name'* by using a connection strategy — the thing you want to remember is a **name**. So the answer is **name**.

audioscript.text: If you have a strategy to help you encode it.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Memory consolidation, the next step in forming an episodic memory, is the process by which memories of encoded information are strengthened, stabilized, and stored to facilitate later retrieval.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Consolidation is most effective when the information being stored can be linked to an existing network of information.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The passage says consolidation works best when information links to *'an existing network of information'* — you add new memories to a **network**. So the answer is **network**.

audioscript.text: Consolidation makes it possible for you to store memories for later retrieval indefinitely.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Forming strong memories depends on the frequency with which you try to retrieve them.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says strong memories depend on *'the frequency with which you try to retrieve them'* — how often you retrieve affects strength. So the answer is **frequency**.

audioscript.text: Memories can fade, or become harder to retrieve if they aren't used very often.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The last step in forming episodic memories is called retrieval, which is the conscious recollection of encoded information.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Retrieving information from episodic memory depends upon semantic, olfactory, auditory, and visual factors.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These help episodic memory retrieval by acting as a prompt, for example.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: When recalling where you parked your car, you may use the color of a sign close to where you parked.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says you may use *'the color of a sign'* as a prompt to remember where you parked — **color** is the visual prompt. So the answer is **color**.

audioscript.text: You actually have to mentally travel back to the moment you parked.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: There are a wide range of neurological diseases and conditions that can affect episodic memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These range from Alzheimer's.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To schizophrenia, to autism.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: An impairment of episodic memory can have a profound effect on individuals' lives, for example.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The symptoms of schizophrenia can be reasonably well controlled by medication.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, patients' episodic memory may still be impaired, and so they are often unable to return to university or work.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Recent studies have shown that computer-assisted games designed to keep the brain active can help improve their episodic memory.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The passage says games designed to *'keep the brain active'* help people with schizophrenia — they stimulate the **brain**. So the answer is **brain**.

audioscript.text: Episodic memories can help people connect with others, for instance, by sharing intimate details about their past.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Something, individuals with autism often have problems with.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This may be caused by an absence of a sense of self.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says autistic children may lack *'a sense of self'*, which is essential for episodic memory — their concept of **self** may be absent. So the answer is **self**.

audioscript.text: This is essential for the storage of episodic memory, and has been found to be impaired in children with autism.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says autistic children may lack *'a sense of self'*, which is essential for episodic memory — their concept of **self** may be absent. So the answer is **self**.

audioscript.text: Research has shown that treatments that improve memory may also have a positive impact on children's social development.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One study looked at...
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: So, if you are one of those people who hasn't found the perfect physical activity yet, here are some things to think about, which might help you make the right decision for you.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The first question to ask yourself is whether you would enjoy training in a gym.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Many people are put off by the idea of having to fit a visit to the gym into their busy day.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: You often have to go very early or late, as some gyms can get very crowded.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But with regular training, you'll see a big difference in a relatively short space of time.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q11: The passage says with regular gym training, you'll see *'a big difference in a relatively short space of time'* — this means you get **fast results**. So the answer is **F**.

audioscript.text: Running has become incredibly popular in recent years.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That's probably got a lot to do with the fact that it's a very accessible form of exercise.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Anyone can run, even if you could only run a few meters to begin with, but make sure you get the right shoes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q12: The passage says *'Anyone can run, even if you could only run a few meters to begin with'* — this means your starting **fitness level is unimportant**. So the answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: It's worth investing in a high quality pair, and they don't come cheap.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Another great thing about running is that you can do it at any time of day or night.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The only thing that may stop you is snow and ice.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Swimming is another really good way to build fitness.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: What attracts many people is that you can swim in an indoor pool at any time of year.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q13: The passage says you can swim in an indoor pool *'at any time of year'* — this means swimming is **not dependent on season**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: On the other hand, it can be quite boring or solitary.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It's hard to chat to people while you're swimming lengths.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Cycling has become almost as popular as running in recent years.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That's probably because as well as improving their fitness, many people say being out in the fresh air in a park or in the countryside can be fun.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says many people find cycling *'fun'* because they are *'out in the fresh air'* — **'fun'** means **enjoyable**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Provided the conditions are right of course, only fanatics go out in the wind and rain.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Yoga is a good choice for those of you looking for exercise, which focuses on developing both a healthy mind and body.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It's a good way of building strength.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And with the right instructor, there's less chance of hurting yourself than with other more active sports.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Especially for people who aren't very flexible.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Getting a personal trainer is a good way to start your fitness program.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Obviously, there can be significant costs involved, but if you've got someone there to encourage you and help you achieve your goals, you're less likely to give up.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Make sure you get someone with a recognized qualification though, or you could do yourself permanent damage.

audioscript.text: Section 3.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear a textile design student called Jim discussing his project on using natural dyes for coloring fabrics with his tutor.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: OK, Jim.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: You wanted to see me about your textile design project.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I've been looking at how a range of natural dyes can be used to color fabrics like cotton and wool.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Why did you choose that topic?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Well, I got a lot of useful ideas from the museum.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: You know, at that exhibition of textiles, but I've always been interested in anything to do with color.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Years ago, I went to a carpet shop with my parents when we were on holiday in Turkey, and I remember all the amazing colors.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q21: The question asks what **first** inspired Jim. He mentions the museum exhibition, but that gave him *'useful ideas'* — not the first inspiration. The real spark came earlier: *'Years ago, I went to a carpet shop with my parents when we were on holiday in Turkey, and I remember all the amazing colors'*. So the answer is **C** — carpets he saw on holiday.

audioscript.text: They might not all have been natural dyes.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Maybe not, but for the project, I decided to follow it up.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: And I found a great book about a botanic garden in California that specializes in plants used for dyes.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: So in your project, you had to include a practical investigation.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yeah, at first I couldn't decide on my variables.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I was going to just look at one type of fiber for example, like cotton, and see how different types of dyes affected it.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Yes.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Then I decided to include others as well, so I looked at cotton and wool and nylon.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q22: Jim says he first thought about looking at *'one type of fiber'* like cotton. But then he changed his mind: *'I decided to include others as well, so I looked at cotton and wool and nylon'*. This means he used **a range of dyes with different fibres** — not just one type. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: With just one type of dye?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Various types, including some that weren't natural for comparison.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: So, I did the experiments last week.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I used some ready made natural dyes.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I found a website which supplied them.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: They came in just a few days, but I also made some of my own.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: That must have taken quite a bit of time.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, I thought it would just be a matter of a teaspoon or so of dye, and actually that wasn't the case at all.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Like I was using one vegetable, beetroot for a red dye.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: And I had to chop up a whole pile of it, so it all took longer than I'd expected.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q23: Jim expected making his own dye would be easy — just *'a teaspoon or so'*. But the passage reveals his surprise: *'I had to chop up a whole pile of it, so it all took longer than I'd expected'*. This means he was surprised by **how much natural material was needed**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: One possibility is to use food colorings.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: I did use one, that was a yellow dye, an artificial one.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Tartrazine?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yeah, I used it on cotton first.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: It came out a great color, but when I rinsed the material, the color just washed away.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q24: Jim tried tartrazine on cotton first. The passage says *'it came out a great color, but when I rinsed the material, the color just washed away'*. This means the dye was **not permanent on cotton** — it disappeared with water. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: I'd been going to try it out on nylon, but I abandoned that idea.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Were you worried about health issues?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: I thought if it's a legal food coloring, it must be safe.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Well, it can occasionally cause allergic reactions, I believe.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: So, what natural dyes did you look at?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Well, one was turmeric.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: The color's great, it's a really strong yellow, it's generally used in dishes like curry.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: It's meant to be quite good for your health when eaten, but you might find it's not permanent when it's used as a dye, a few washes and it's gone.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q25: The tutor warns Jim about turmeric: *'you might find it's not permanent when it's used as a dye, a few washes and it's gone'*. **'Not permanent'** means the colour does not last. So the problem is **C** — the colour is not long-lasting.

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I used beetroot as a dye for wool.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: When I chop up beetroot to eat, I always end up with bright red hands, but the wool ended up just a sort of watery cream shade, disappointing.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q26: Jim expected beetroot to give a strong red colour, but the result was different: *'the wool ended up just a sort of watery cream shade, disappointing'*. The colour he got was not what he expected. So the problem is **F** — the colour may be unexpected.

audioscript.text: There's a natural dye called Tyrian purple, have you heard of that?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yes.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: It comes from a shellfish, and it was worn in ancient times, but only by important people, as it was so rare.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q27: The passage says Tyrian purple *'was worn in ancient times, but only by important people, as it was so rare'*. **'Rare'** means it is hard to find. Jim also says *'I didn't use it'*. So the problem is **H** — it is not generally available.

audioscript.text: I didn't use it.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: It fell out of use centuries ago, though one researcher managed to get hold of some recently. But that shade of purple can be produced by chemical dyes nowadays.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Did you use any black dyes?
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Logwood.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: That was quite complicated.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I had to prepare the fabric so the dye would take.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I hope you were careful to wear gloves.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, I know the danger with that dye.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Good, it can be extremely dangerous if it's ingested.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q28: The tutor warns Jim about logwood: *'it can be extremely dangerous if it's ingested'*. **'Extremely dangerous'** means it is very harmful to the body. So the problem is **D** — it is very poisonous.

audioscript.text: Now presumably you had a look at an insect based dye like cochineal for example.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, I didn't actually make that.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: I didn't have time to start crushing up insects to get the red color.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: And anyway they're not available here, but I managed to get the dye quite easily from a website, but it cost a fortune.
audioscript.speaker: JIM
audioscript.explain: Q29: Jim says he got cochineal from a website, but *'it cost a fortune'*. **'Cost a fortune'** means it was very expensive. So the problem is **A** — it is expensive.

audioscript.text: I can see why it's generally just used in cooking and in small quantities.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Yes, it's very effective, but that's precisely why it's not used as a dye.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: I also read about using metal oxide.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Apparently you can allow iron to rust while it's in contact with the fabric.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: And that colors it.
audioscript.speaker: JIM

audioscript.text: Yes, that works well for dyeing cotton, but you have to be careful as the metal can actually affect the fabric, and so you can't expect to get a lot of wear out of fabrics treated in this way.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR
audioscript.explain: Q30: The tutor explains that with metal oxide, *'the metal can actually affect the fabric, and so you can't expect to get a lot of wear out of fabrics treated in this way'*. This means the metal harms the material over time. So the problem is **E** — it can damage the fabric.

audioscript.text: And the colors are quite subtle, not everyone likes them.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: Anyway, it looks as if you've done a lot of work.
audioscript.speaker: TUTOR

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 3.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

audioscript.text: Last week we started looking at reptiles, including crocodiles and snakes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Today, I'd like us to have a look at another reptile, the lizard, and in particular at some studies that have been done on a particular type of lizard, whose Latin name is Tiliqua rugosa.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This is commonly known as the sleepy lizard, because it's quite slow in its movements and spends quite a lot of its time dozing under rocks or lying in the sun.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I'll start with a general description.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Sleepy lizards live in Western and South Australia, where they're quite common.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Unlike European lizards, which are mostly small, green and fast-moving,
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: sleepy lizards are brown, but what's particularly distinctive about them is the color of their tongue, which is dark blue, in contrast with the lining of their mouth which is bright pink.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says *'what's particularly distinctive about them is the color of their tongue, which is dark blue'* — **'distinctive'** means **'recognisable'**. So the answer is **tongue**.

audioscript.text: And they're much bigger than most European lizards.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They have quite a varied diet, including insects and even small animals, but they mostly eat plants of varying kinds.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says *'they mostly eat plants of varying kinds'* — **'mostly'** means **'mainly'**. So the answer is **plants**.

audioscript.text: Even though they're quite large and powerful, with strong jaws that can crush beetles and snail shells, they still have quite a few predators.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Large birds like cassowaries were one of the main ones in the past.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But nowadays, they're more likely to be caught and killed by snakes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage says *'nowadays, they're more likely to be caught and killed by snakes'* — **'caught and killed by'** means **'predators'**. So the answer is **snakes**.

audioscript.text: Actually, another threat to their survival isn't a predator at all, but is man made.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Quite a large number of sleepy lizards are killed by cars when they're trying to cross highways.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One study carried out by Michael Freake at Flinders University investigated the methods of navigation of these lizards.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Though they move slowly, they can travel quite long distances.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And he found that even if they were taken some distance away from their home territory, they could usually find their way back home as long as they could see the sky.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says *'they could usually find their way back home as long as they could see the sky'* — **'find their way'** means **'navigate'**. So the answer is **sky**.

audioscript.text: They didn't need any other landmarks on the ground.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Observations of these lizards in the wild have also revealed that their mating habits are quite unusual.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Unlike most animals, it seems that they're relatively monogamous, returning to the same partner year after year.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage says *'returning to the same partner year after year'* — **'year after year'** means **'for several years'**. So the answer is **partner**.

audioscript.text: And the male and female also stay together for a long time, both before and after the birth of their young.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It's quite interesting to think about the possible reasons for this.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It could be that it's to do with protecting their young.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: You'd expect them to have a much better chance of survival.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: If they have both parents around, but in fact, observers have noted that once the babies have hatched out of their eggs, they have hardly any contact with their parents.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The passage says *'once the babies have hatched... they have hardly any contact with their parents'* — **'hardly any'** means **'little'**. So the answer is **contact**.

audioscript.text: So there's not really any evidence to support that idea.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Another suggestion's based on the observation that male lizards in monogamous relationships tend to be bigger and stronger than other males.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So maybe the male lizards stay around, so they can give the female lizards protection from other males.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says *'so they can give the female lizards protection from other males'* — **'give... protection'** means **'provide protection'**. So the answer is **protection**.

audioscript.text: But again, we're not really sure.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Finally, I'd like to mention another study that involved collecting data by tracking the lizards.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I was actually involved in this myself, so we caught some lizards in the wild.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And we developed a tiny GPS system that would allow us to track them, and we fixed this onto their tails.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says *'we fixed this onto their tails'* — **'this'** refers to the **GPS system**. So the answer is **tail**.

audioscript.text: Then we set the lizards free again, and we were able to track them for 12 days and gather data, not just about their location, but even about how many steps they took during this period.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The passage says *'even about how many steps they took during this period'* — **'how many steps they took'** means **'the number of steps'**. So the answer is **steps**.

audioscript.text: One surprising thing we discovered from this is that there were far fewer meetings between lizards than we expected.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It seems that they were actually trying to avoid one another.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So why would that be?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Well, again, we have no clear evidence, but one hypothesis is that male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says *'male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another'* and *'this avoidance is a way of preventing this'* — **'preventing'** means **'reduce chances of'**. So the answer is **injury**.

audioscript.text: So maybe this avoidance is a way of preventing this, of self preservation if you like.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says *'male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another'* and *'this avoidance is a way of preventing this'* — **'preventing'** means **'reduce chances of'**. So the answer is **injury**.

audioscript.text: But we need to collect a lot more data before we can be sure of any of this.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER
